description:
SURFACED by fz-rh2.16.5 (runtime/interp parity) investigation. enum_predicate_search was listed there as an fz2 INTERP parity gap, but diagnosis proved it is NOT interp-only: it fails IDENTICALLY on all three backends (fz2 run / interp / build) with the same ValueId/FunctionId, symptom "native attempted to materialize absent value as runtime value" / "backend value N is unbound". So it is a compiler2 specialization/demand-modeling bug, not a runtime/interp parity issue -- out of scope for fz-rh2.16.5 (whose hard rule keeps runtime/interp fixes separate from planning-layer bugs), and correctly left red there.

MINIMAL REPRO (no panic/early-exit needed): two call sites of the SAME generic Enum higher-order function with DIFFERENT closures already breaks -- e.g. two Enum.find/3 calls with different predicates, or Enum.find/3 + Enum.find_value/3 together. One call site works; the second distinct-closure specialization reaches the backend referencing a value that was never materialized ("backend value N is unbound").

This is the same class as the specialization/demand family (fz-xqw SpecKey/BodyKey planner split; the just-closed fz-hwn runtime-demand work grounded dispatch surfaces but this monomorphization/value-materialization gap survives). Likely locus: activation specialization keying / demand-derived value materialization when one generic body is specialized at 2+ distinct closure surfaces, where a per-specialization value is demanded by one path but not materialized for the other.

FIX then unblocks matrix promotion of enum_predicate_search on all three fz2 paths (feeds fz-rh2.16.1 promotion / fz-rh2.16.6 deletion keystone). Verify: the two-distinct-closure repro runs green on run/interp/build; enum_predicate_search fixture green all paths; lib+matrix green. Related: fz-rh2.16.5, fz-xqw, fz-hwn.
title: Generic Enum HOF specialized at 2+ distinct closures leaves a backend value unbound (all backends: run/interp/build)
